A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ctrl-World and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Matching content across pagination changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original world-model evaluations, component ablations, comparisons with real robot rollouts, and policy fine-tuning results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds multi-view baseline results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The multi-view architecture, pose-conditioned memory, frame-level action conditioning, diffusion objective, and policy-improvement procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B's adapter and forward-kinematics procedure are also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use DROID, the same seven policy-evaluation tasks, and the same four policy-improvement categories. The added baseline configurations introduce no new datasets, tasks, or environments.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds WPE-Multiview and IRASim-Multiview alongside the existing single-view comparisons. WPE and IRASim receive explicit Single-View labels, while Ctrl-World-Third-View becomes Ctrl-World-Single-View; these retained rows are not new methods.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds multi-view configurations of the two baselines under the existing third-view evaluation. The stated 2% validation holdout, 256 ten-second clips, action chunks, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Details of the new configurations are unspecified.

E4.justification: Table 2's memory, frame-level conditioning, and joint-prediction ablations remain unchanged, as do the controllability, attention, and consistency analyses in Figures 4–5. The new Table 1 entries extend comparator results without a separately developed ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: There are no changes to run or seed disclosure, uncertainty reporting, or statistical testing. Table 1 retains averaging over 256 clips, and the added rows use the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports PSNR/FVD of 21.17/147.1 for WPE-Multiview and 20.21/165.4 for IRASim-Multiview; their other three metrics are unreported. All existing numerical results, including the ablations and appendix policy results, are retained.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations 1–3, and appendix adapter and kinematics equations are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable multi-view simulation, long-horizon consistency, policy-ranking alignment, and policy improvement. The reported improvement from 38.7% to 83.4% is present in both versions.

C2.justification: Explanations of memory retrieval, multi-view consistency, and controllability remain unchanged. Both versions retain limitations concerning precise physics, missed retries, initial-observation sensitivity, and improving low-level execution. The added baseline results receive no new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Sections 5.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same architecture details, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, and reported code/video access information. No implementation or training details are added for the new multi-view baselines.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Huang, Hafner, Ren, Jiang, and He et al. (2025), and Li et al. (2024), with citations covering related world models, action conditioning, and simulation-based evaluation. The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header, inserts citations, and revises Table 1 method labels. Section order and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged; apparent paragraph moves mainly reflect pagination.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from four to six method rows and updates row labels. Figures 1–9 and Tables 2–7 retain their content and design, with limited layout reflow and added publication headers.

improvement.justification: The added multi-view comparator results make Table 1 more informative about alternatives to Ctrl-World, while additional citations improve attribution. The gain is limited: the new variants lack implementation details and three of five metrics, and Section 5.2 still describes the baselines as single-view. The method, central empirical evidence, and appendices otherwise remain unchanged.
